Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zutable 0.0.0.9000

  • zutable_info() reports the package version.
  • Every condition the package raises inherits from zutable_error.
  • schema(), field() and not_null() describe a table’s columns with Arrow’s logical types: int32, float64, string, date, timestamp(unit, tz), decimal(p, s), enum(levels), list(type), struct(...) and more, read inside the call so they mask nothing. schema() of a data frame infers its types.
  • A POSIXct with no time zone is typed timestamp("us", "UTC").
  • na(type) gives a typed missing value, for placeholders.
  • register_extension_type() lets a package type its vector class as an Arrow extension.
  • zutable() and as_zutable() create typed tables: plain data frames that carry their schema and print it under the column names. Values enter exactly or not at all.
  • conform() checks a table against a schema and lists every mismatch; metadata() returns a table’s key-value pairs.
  • Base R’s value forms (x[i, ], x[, j], x$col) work, so head(), subset(), split() and unique() return zutables. No replacement changes a table’s schema: a value must fit its column’s type, and renaming or removing a column is an error.
  • Expressions are written in a closed, typed vocabulary of SQL-named functions with R synonyms (?vocabulary): arithmetic, comparison, logic, strings, patterns, dates, cast(), case(), aggregates, and r() to run arbitrary R. Every expression is typed before any data is read, and every function gives the same result locally and in DuckDB.
  • The bracket takes SQL’s clauses as named arguments: where, select (with .all and -name), order (with desc()), limit and distinct, run in SQL’s logical order. x[cond, .(...)] reads as in data.table, and a position that mentions no column is a value form.
  • explain() prints the plan that made a table, one step per line; dplyr::explain() reaches it too.

Developed by Pedro Baltazar.
